title: Why does a protractor have two sets of numbers?
description: A protractor shows one set of numbers growing from right to left and another growing from left to right. A sharp angle is read with its base arm on the right zero and again on the left zero, to see why both sets are there. Keeko's doubt, that one set is enough, is broken by reading the wrong set and getting a big number for a sharp angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the set of numbers whose zero lies on the base arm. Watch for children who always read the same set whichever arm is the base.

source: Will these (the numbers written on the protractor) make it e
video_script.why: The child learns why a protractor has two sets of numbers and which set to read for an angle.
video_script.substitution: The book's labelled protractor, with a sharp angle laid first with its base arm on the right zero and then on the left zero.
video_script.anchor: the book's labelled protractor with two sets of numbers, one growing from right to left and one from left to right
video_script.wrong_answer: always read the same set of numbers
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says always read the same set of numbers, because one set is enough. When the base arm sits at the other end, that set gives a large number for a sharp angle, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The two sets let you start from either arm. Read the set whose zero is on the base arm.

final_answer.value: the two sets of numbers let you start from either arm as the zero line; read the set whose zero lies on the base arm
final_answer.spoken: the two sets let you start from either arm, and you read the set whose zero is on the base arm

hold_back: the set whose zero is on the base arm
maths_rules: one set of numbers has 0 on the right and grows from right to left, up to 180 on the left
the other set has 0 on the left and grows from left to right, up to 180 on the right
a sharp angle with its base arm on the right zero crosses 50 on the set that starts at the right zero, and 130 on the other set
the same sharp angle with its base arm on the left zero crosses 50 on the set that starts at the left zero, and 130 on the other set
the two readings for one angle add up to 180, and the sharp one is smaller than 90, so the set whose zero is on the base arm is the right one
video_script.design: One protractor stays on the board. The same sharp angle is laid on it twice, once with each arm as the base arm, and the two sets of numbers are lit in two colours.

<bookmark mark='half'/>A half circle divided into one hundred and eighty equal parts is called a protractor.
<bookmark mark='sets'/>It has two sets of numbers, one growing from right to left and one from left to right.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Why does it need two sets?
